title: The alpha and beta augmentation boundary squares
statement: Let X be a scheme, U_i arbitrary opens, T a short exact sequence of abelian sheaves surjective on every tuple intersection, and q a natural number. Choose prescribed end resolutions I₁ and I₃. Let e₁ and e₃ identify Ext with section homology in degrees q+1 and q, with the cocycle representative property of [lem-pc-abelian-cech-ext-section-iso]. There exists a homomorphism δ from degree-q total homology of I₃ to degree-(q+1) total homology of I₁ such that δ_Cech followed by H(beta₁) equals H(beta₃) followed by δ, and δ_Ext followed by e₁ and H(alpha₁) equals e₃ followed by H(alpha₃) and δ. The explicit augmentations and total complexes are those of [def-pc-abelian-cech-comparison-construction]. No canonical comparison map c or d is assumed and no cover hypothesis is needed.

source.place: Functorial long exact cohomology sequence, together with Tag 013T prescribed horseshoe and Tag 01EQ augmentations

proof.text: Apply the proved prescribed-horseshoe theorem. Map each row splitting through global sections; injectivity of the first resolution term supplies a splitting. Degreewise short exactness gives the section short exact sequence S.
Apply the proved horseshoe total-boundary theorem to obtain delta and the beta and section-alpha boundary squares.

Apply the Ext/section boundary identification to the given cocycle-compatible e1 and e3. Compose its equation with H(alpha1), reassociate, and substitute the section-alpha square. Pair this result with the beta square.

proof_origin.place: Prescribed horseshoe, proved section exactness and total augmentation naturality; Ext/section boundary identification isolated; Lean composition by C2

theorem abelianCechAugmentation_boundary_squares
    {X : Scheme.{u}} {ι : Type u} (U : ι → X.Opens)
    (T : ShortComplex (Sheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}))
    (hT : T.ShortExact)
    (hg : ∀ (k : ℕ) (y : Fin (k + 1) → ι),
      Function.Surjective (T.g.hom.app (op (⨅ l, U (y l))))) (q : ℕ)
    (I₁ : InjectiveResolution T.X₁) (I₃ : InjectiveResolution T.X₃)
    (e₁ : (Sheaf.functorH (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (q + 1)).obj T.X₁ ≅
      (abelianCechSections I₁).homology (q + 1))
    (e₃ : (Sheaf.functorH (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) q).obj T.X₃ ≅
      (abelianCechSections I₃).homology q)
    (he₁ : ∀ (t : (Sheaf.functorH (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) (q + 1)).obj T.X₁),
      ∃ (a : (constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
          (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)) ⟶ I₁.cocomplex.X (q + 1))
        (ha : a ≫ I₁.cocomplex.d (q + 1) ((q + 1) + 1) = 0)
        (z : (abelianCechSections I₁).cycles (q + 1)),
        I₁.extMk a ((q + 1) + 1) rfl ha = t ∧
        ((constantSheafAdj (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
          isTerminalTop).homEquiv _ _ a) (ULift.up 1) =
            (abelianCechSections I₁).iCycles (q + 1) z ∧
        e₁.hom t = (abelianCechSections I₁).homologyπ (q + 1) z)
    (he₃ : ∀ (t : (Sheaf.functorH (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) q).obj T.X₃),
      ∃ (a : (constantSheaf (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}).obj
          (AddCommGrpCat.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)) ⟶ I₃.cocomplex.X q)
        (ha : a ≫ I₃.cocomplex.d q (q + 1) = 0)
        (z : (abelianCechSections I₃).cycles q),
        I₃.extMk a (q + 1) rfl ha = t ∧
        ((constantSheafAdj (Opens.grothendieckTopology X) AddCommGrpCat.{u}
          isTerminalTop).homEquiv _ _ a) (ULift.up 1) =
            (abelianCechSections I₃).iCycles q z ∧
        e₃.hom t = (abelianCechSections I₃).homologyπ q z) :
    ∃ (δ : ((abelianCechDouble U I₃).total (.up ℕ)).homology q ⟶
        ((abelianCechDouble U I₁).total (.up ℕ)).homology (q + 1)),
      TopCat.Sheaf.cechδ U hT hg q ≫
          HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (abelianCechBeta U I₁) (q + 1) =
        HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (abelianCechBeta U I₃) q ≫ δ ∧
      Sheaf.functorHδ hT q ≫ e₁.hom ≫
          HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (abelianCechAlpha U I₁) (q + 1) =
        e₃.hom ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (abelianCechAlpha U I₃) q ≫ δ
